facts.statement: Microsteus was a small genus of arthrodire placoderms belonging to the family Selenosteidae.
facts.quote: Microsteus is an extinct genus of small selenosteid arthrodire placoderms

facts.statement: Fossils of Microsteus have been found in the Upper Frasnian Kellwasserkalk facies of Germany.
facts.quote: known from the Upper Frasnian Kellwasserkalk facies of Late Devonian Germany

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Microsteus is Microsteus dubius.
The genus Microsteus includes three species: M. dubius, M. angusticeps, and M. gracilis.
facts.quote: subdivision: Microsteus dubius Gross 1932 Microsteus angusticeps (Stensiö 1963) Microsteus gracilis (Stensiö 1963)

facts.statement: The species M. angusticeps and M. gracilis were originally classified in the genus Parawalterosteus.
facts.quote: M. angusticeps and M. gracilis originally composed the genus Parawalterosteus

facts.statement: It is debated whether M. angusticeps and M. gracilis are distinct species or should be merged with M. dubius.
facts.quote: Denison (1978) suggests that M. angusticeps and M. gracilis do not have enough differences from M. dubius to merit separate species status, but other authors, such as Rücklin 2011, treat the three as separate species

facts.statement: Microsteus lived during the Frasnian stage, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 372.15 million years ago)
